title: Thiruparankundram lamp lit at old spot, not hilltop pillar the Supreme Court allowed; contempt plea next
dek: Tamil Nadu kept the Karthigai Deepam at the Uchi Pillaiyar mandapam despite a one-time Supreme Court nod for the Deepathoon; BJP chief Nainar Nagenthran was stopped and petitioners say they will seek contempt.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Karthigai Deepam was lit at its customary spot on Thiruparankundram hill near Madurai on Tuesday evening, not at the hilltop stone pillar where the Supreme Court had allowed a one-time lighting this year, setting up a contempt fight between Hindu petitioners and Tamil Nadu's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government.

A small team of priests from the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy temple lit the Maha Deepam at the Uchi Pillaiyar Deepa Mandapam, as in past years, while police guarded the Deepathoon pillar near the summit, according to reports. Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran was stopped on his way to the hill, police removed protesters at the foothills after the ceremony, and the petitioners' lawyer said he would now ask the Supreme Court to begin contempt proceedings.

## What happened

The Supreme Court's order of 20 November allowed the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon on 24 November, the day of the festival, as what the bench called a temporary, one-time arrangement. Under the order, the Madurai District Collector was the nodal officer and was to settle the composition of the lighting team with the temple's executive officer, the Archaeological Survey of India and the city police commissioner. No members of the public were to go with the team, and observances at customary locations were to continue undisturbed. The lighting was set for 6 pm, according to reports.

In the event, the lamp was lit only at the mandapam. Police were deployed beside the pillar, where an electric light was seen, reports said. In a joint statement after the ceremony, the temple's executive officer, G. Selvi, and the chairman of its board of trustees, V. Shanmugasundaram, said the lighting followed "longstanding custom and Agama rules" and was part of a ritual the temple has observed for generations, according to reports.

Earlier in the day the Madurai Collector, Nishanth Krishna, told the Madras High Court's Madurai bench that the district administration was taking steps to comply with the Supreme Court's order, reports said. A bench of Justices G.R. Swaminathan and M.D. Sumathi asked the Collector, the police commissioner and the temple authorities to comply, and held that the Collector's prohibitory order could not stand in the way of devotees' fundamental rights. In a separate order, the High Court restrained members of the public from calling for defiance of the Supreme Court's order.

The prohibitory orders, in force from 9 pm on 23 November to 10 am on 25 November, banned gatherings, rallies and unauthorised climbing of the hill, and the police declared the area a temporary no-drone zone. Reports put the police deployment at between about 5,600 and 6,000 personnel.

## Detentions and protests

Mr Nagenthran was stopped at a check post in Tirunelveli district on Tuesday afternoon while travelling to Thiruparankundram; reports variously described him as arrested, detained or placed under house arrest. BJP leaders and members of the Hindu Munnani were held in several districts. Reports differ on the scale: one said the state put the number detained across Tamil Nadu at 258, while BJP functionaries said about 750 party leaders were held under house arrest.

At the foothills, BJP members and Hindu Munnani activists argued with police outside the Murugan temple, and police removed protesters after the ceremony, according to reports. There was a scuffle between the BJP leader S.G. Surya and police. In Chennai, Hindu Munnani members protested on the road outside Central railway station, holding up traffic.

## Background

The dispute is over where the lamp should be lit. Thiruparankundram hill is home both to the Murugan temple at its base and to the Sikandar Badusha dargah at its summit; the Deepathoon is a stone pillar about 50 metres from the dargah. Successive state governments, under both the DMK and the AIADMK, have kept the lighting at the Uchi Pillaiyar mandapam, part-way up the hill.

In late 2025 a single judge of the High Court allowed the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon. The then DMK government refused, citing law and order, and the district administration imposed prohibitory orders; a High Court bench later found that its order had been wilfully disobeyed and ordered central security forces to provide protection. On 6 January 2026 a Division Bench upheld the single judge's ruling and rejected the state's argument that the pillar was a survey stone from British rule.

The TVK government, which took office this year under Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, kept the previous government's position. It filed an appeal in the Supreme Court on 11 June and said in June that it would hold the ritual at the usual location, putting social harmony first, according to reports. On 20 November the Supreme Court bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi stayed the High Court's findings while it hears the appeal, but allowed this year's one-time lighting, saying the arrangement neither accepted nor rejected either side's arguments. The state's Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) commissioner filed a petition the same day asking the court to review that interim order, according to reports.

## What they are saying

RM Arun Swaminathan, the lawyer for the petitioner Rama Ravikumar, said the administration had left no choice. "Now there is no other option except to file a contempt application," he said, according to reports. He accused the state government of bias against Hindus and said he might also raise perjury and ask the court to act on its own.

Mr Nagenthran has accused the TVK of copying what he calls the DMK's anti-Hindu stance on the issue. The Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), part of the TVK government, has strongly opposed lighting the lamp at the Deepathoon, and its leader Thol. Thirumavalavan had said the state would light it at the mandapam. The Left parties, which support the government from outside, share that position, according to reports. TVK ministers had been non-committal before the festival, and The Declaration could not find a statement from the state government on Tuesday's decision by early Wednesday.

## What happens next

The petitioners plan to move the Supreme Court for contempt. The state's review petition against the interim order is pending, and the court has yet to hear the main appeal against the High Court's January judgment, which will decide whether there is any customary right to light the lamp at the pillar in future years.

## Timeline

- 6 Jan 2026: High Court Division Bench upholds order allowing lighting at the Deepathoon
- 11 Jun 2026: TVK government appeals to the Supreme Court
- 20 Nov 2026: Supreme Court stays High Court findings but allows a one-time lighting on 24 November; state seeks review
- 24 Nov 2026: Lamp lit at the Uchi Pillaiyar mandapam; petitioners say they will seek contempt
